download-failure-detail-is-the-fetch-cat: The TS downloader rejected with its own message ('Download failed with Error: socket hang up', 'Download failed with Error: Download stopped or paused') and the engine carried it as the detail of a download-failed or aborted result. The Rust Fetch seam never reports a transport message, a URL or a header (T-87-09); a failure is a category word ('network', 'status(404)', 'aborted', 'io') and that word is the detail. The reason, the aborted flag and the status sequence are unchanged; only the detail text differs, in the three goldens that script a failing download (download-failed-network, download-stopped-without-signal, abort-during-download-progress).
extract-failure-log-names-no-tar-output: When tar failed the TS extractFiles logged 'Extracting Error: <tar stderr>' at error level. The engine log carries fixed text only and never a profile path or a child's output (T-86-15, the same rule as gamelib-info), so the Rust engine logs 'Engine: tar exited with an error' at error level and returns the same 'dxvk: tar failed' or 'wine: tar failed' detail to the caller. The replay maps the golden's line to the Rust one; nothing on disk, no result and no event differs.
removal-goes-through-the-safety-guard: The TS removed the temp directory of an install, an engine directory being replaced and every unpinned engine with rmSync recursive, after a lexical containment test. Rust removes each of them through gamelib_safety::remove::remove_tree with <appFolder>/tools/steam-engines as the trust root (D-19, FND-02): a target outside the root, the root itself, a path with a dot segment and a root the guard cannot resolve (unknown) delete nothing, and a symlink is unlinked with its referent never opened. Where the TS would have deleted and the guard refuses, the directory stays and a warning names it; no golden reaches that branch because every golden directory is inside the root, and the guard test in golden_fallback.rs pins the refusals instead.
unavailable-log-line-names-the-reason-no: The TS reporter logged 'built-in engine unavailable for <runner> <app>: <reason> <detail>' at warning level. A detail can carry a path (the symlink escape names the offending link under the profile), and the engine log never carries one (T-86-15), so the Rust line names the reason only; the full detail is in the result the caller receives, as before. The replay cuts the golden's line to the reason.
